---
title: Navigation
---

## Overview

HTML pages rendered with Quarto can include a table of contents that
tracks the section structure of the document and lets readers jump to
any section. This page covers the table of contents options; for
site-level navigation (navbars, sidebars, breadcrumbs), see the
[websites guides](../projects/create.qmd).

## Table of Contents

Enable the table of contents with the `toc` option:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
---
```

By default the table of contents shows headings up to level 3 and
renders in the right margin of the page. You can control both:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
toc-depth: 4
toc-title: Contents
---
```

- `toc-depth` sets the deepest heading level included (default: 3).
- `toc-title` sets the heading shown above the table of contents
  (default: "Table of contents", localized to the document language).

## Following the reader

As the page scrolls, the entry for the current section is highlighted,
and nested entries open around it: by default only the top level is
shown, plus the branch that holds the current section. Use `toc-expand`
to show more (or less) of the tree from the start:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
toc-expand: 2
---
```

| Value   | Behavior                                                   |
|---------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `1`     | The default: top-level entries, plus the current branch    |
| `N`     | Entries down to level `N` stay open; deeper ones follow the reader |
| `true`  | Every entry is always open                                 |
| `false` | Nested entries are shown only while their section is current |

The tracking is a small script shipped with the page
(`quarto-toc.js`). Without JavaScript the table of contents is a plain
list with its first entry marked as current. A page script can listen
for the `quarto-sectionChanged` event on `window`, which fires whenever
the current section changes.

## Replacing the table of contents with a component

To render the table of contents yourself, point `toc-component` at a
React component, written the same way as any
[component](components.qmd):

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
toc-component: my-toc.tsx
---
```

The component is mounted over the `nav#TOC` element in place of the
default script, and receives:

- `props`: the table of contents as data, typed as `QuartoTocProps` in
  the `@quarto/components` package: `title`, `entries` (each with `id`,
  `title`, `level`, `number` and `children`), `expanded` (the
  `toc-expand` value as a number, or `null`) and `location`;
- `children`: the default markup (the title, the list, and any
  repository action links), which a component can render as-is or
  replace;
- `host`: the `nav` element.

``` tsx
import type { QuartoComponentProps, QuartoTocProps } from "@quarto/components";

export default function Toc({ props }: QuartoComponentProps<QuartoTocProps>) {
  return (
    <ol>
      {props.entries.map((e) => (
        <li key={e.id}><a href={`#${e.id}`}>{e.title}</a></li>
      ))}
    </ol>
  );
}
```

Without JavaScript the page shows the default list. The option is
inert on pages that render no table of contents, like `toc-location`.

::: callout-note
The q2 preview shows the default table of contents for a page that sets
`toc-component`; mounting the component in the preview is planned.
:::

## Location

Use `toc-location` to choose where the table of contents appears:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
toc-location: left
---
```

The available locations:

| Value   | Placement                                             |
|---------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `right` | In the right margin (the default)                     |
| `left`  | In a sidebar to the left of the document body         |
| `body`  | In the document body, above the content               |

On pages of a website project, `toc-location: left` places the table
of contents inside the site's navigation sidebar — after the
navigation entries when the page has a sidebar, or on its own when it
does not.

On narrow screens the left and right table-of-contents sidebars are
hidden; use `toc-location: body` if the table of contents should
remain visible at every screen size.

::: callout-note
The `left-body` and `right-body` values (which show the table of
contents both in a sidebar and in the body) are not supported yet;
they currently fall back to `left` and `right` respectively, with a
warning.
:::
